English: Clay Catchment
A rudimentary pit dug in clay-rich soil to capture precious rainfall, allowing nomads to survive dry spells.
Wooden Trough
Simple troughs made of local timber, supporting basic water storage and livestock needs for the moving clan.
Stone Basin
A durable, stone-lined basin for rainwater collection, protecting supply from evaporation and contamination.
Rain Collector
A sophisticated collection system using sloped surfaces and channels, maximizing the capture of seasonal rains.
Guarded Tank
A fortified water tank with guards and fencing, protecting the vital supply from theft and contamination.
Filtered Pavilion
A tented structure with sand and gravel filtering, providing cleaner water and boosting the health and unity of the clan.
Covered Reservoir
A large, roofed reservoir that shields precious water from the sun and dust storms, ensuring clan survival in the harshest seasons.
Expanded Tank
A massive, stone-lined tank with multiple compartments, capable of supporting large gatherings and livestock herds.
Community Water Hall
A grand communal hall built beside the tank, doubling as a council meeting place and water distribution center, strengthening unity and prestige.
East African Rain Tank
The ultimate feat of engineering for nomads: a vast, protected water system that sustains the mightiest of clans and inspires awe among all who see it.
